evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: This story establishes the game concept and does not depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators inherently requires a game to invite them to, which is created by PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round requires an existing game, which is created by PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displaying all items depends on items being entered or added, which is provided by PP-003 and PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires an existing list of items, established through PP-003 and PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item inherently assumes an existing item list and session, established by PP-003 and displayed by PP-004.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing requires an existing item in the list, which is created via PP-003 or PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting requires an existing item in the list, which is created via PP-003 or PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates requires an active item selected for estimation, which is provided by PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires estimates to exist for a selected item, which depends on PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: estimate field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatic estimate population requires an active estimation round for a selected item, which depends on PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed-upon estimate requires a selected item being estimated, provided by PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a story depends on earlier estimation of that story, which requires PP-003, PP-005, and PP-012.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: This provides an independent input path for stories and does not require manual item entry stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: This is an alternative independent input mechanism and does not require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires games to exist, which is established by PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on games and estimation activity, initially established by PP-001 and PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires transcript data to exist, which is provided by PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires transcript data to exist, which is provided by PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game requires a game to exist, which is created by PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: This story establishes the account concept and does not depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login requires an account to exist, which is created by PP-021.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account, which is created by PP-021.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires an existing account, which is created by PP-021.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone formatting is a cross-cutting display concern and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require an existing account with stored email, which is created by PP-021.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an estimation scale is a self-contained configuration choice and does not clearly require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invitations depends on the estimator invitation capability defined in PP-002.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game requires an existing game and invitation URL, established by PP-001 and PP-002.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: This requires a selected item for the current estimation round, provided by PP-003 and PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items depends on the item list, established through PP-003 and PP-004.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given
evaluations.rationale: This requires an active item being estimated, which depends on PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates depends on an active estimation round for a selected item, provided by PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate requires an active estimate draw for a selected item, which depends on PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Prior estimates only exist after estimation activity on a selected story, depending on PP-005 and PP-012.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying estimates by estimator depends on an active estimation round, which requires PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset depends on the timer feature from PP-037 and on estimates being played.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds requires prior stories and estimates, which depend on PP-003, PP-005, and PP-012.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Consistent card ordering is a self-contained presentation behavior and does not require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate requires an active draw for a selected item, which depends on PP-005.

evaluations.evidence: small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail photo is a self-contained UI feature and does not require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A definitions list is a self-contained reference feature.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is a technical performance measure and not a concrete requirement-level dependency on another story.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browser compatibility is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance is a non-functional requirement and does not constitute a concrete dependency on another story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a cross-cutting input capability and does not depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained usability requirement and does not require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a self-contained cross-cutting feature and do not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Non-identifiable storage is a self-contained data handling requirement and does not require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics viewing can be implemented as an independent reporting feature; there is no concrete prerequisite story in the backlog.
